image_prompt.text: Crisp white touchlines and goal lines drawn around the green rectangular pitch, a single flat rectangle of play at the centre of the track
A white centre circle and centre spot painted at midfield on the green field
Two simple low-poly goal frames in flat white, one centred on each end line of the pitch
Flat white lane stripes running the length of the oval track and simple straight markings across the field, all plain painted lines with no texture
An oval running track in flat reddish-brown tan encircling the central field, built from simple geometric segments — two straights and two curved ends

layout_placement.text: A detection perimeter along the touchlines and goal lines of the pitch so play stops the moment the ball or a player crosses out
The centre spot the ball resets to for kickoff, with the two team start positions either side of the halfway line
A scoring plane across each goal mouth registering a point when the ball passes between the posts

notes: Whole build is low-poly minimalist: flat single colours, simple geometric shapes, no textures or detail geometry. This is an art-direction constraint on every pick rather than a placeable feature, so it is recorded here instead of as a list entry.

The oval running track has no option in Sports and is carried as free text in image_prompt. Racing was considered as a second genre for it and rejected: the prompt states no laps, finish line, or competition, so the track is stadium geometry rather than a race circuit, and naming Racing would have imported a genre it does not lead.
"Two simple goal posts at each end" is recorded as count 2 read as one goal frame per end line, the standard soccer-pitch reading. If the user meant two separate frames at each end, the count is 4.

Stadium dressing from the Full Stadium preset (bleachers, enclosure wall, team sectors) was deliberately left out — the prompt lists exactly four elements and asks for minimalism, and spectator-bleachers would have added tiered elevation nobody asked for.

would have asked: Sounds like a bounded pitch: white touchlines and goal lines around the green rectangle, a centre circle to restart play from, and a goal at each end that registers a score — plus the tan oval running track ringing the whole thing, all in flat low-poly colour. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: is the running track just geometry to look at, or does it need per-lane markings and a start/finish line so players can actually race on it? Built it as plain lane-striped geometry for now.

would have asked: should the pitch markings be a full regulation set (penalty boxes, corner arcs) or only the outline, centre circle, and halfway line? Took the minimal set, since you asked for simple lines.
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?
